questions.question: What is the chemical name of ‘oil of vitriol’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulfuric acid / sulphuric acid.**__

__
 
• Sulfuric acid is a dense, colourless, oily, corrosive liquid.
 
• It is one of the most commercially important of all chemicals. 
 
• It is prepared industrially by the reaction of water with sulfur trioxide.
 
• Vitriol is any of certain hydrated sulfates or sulfuric acid.
 
• Uses of** Sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄):**
 
 
• In lead storage battery.
 
• In the manufacturing of HCl.
 
• In the manufacturing of Alum.
 
• In the manufacturing of fertilisers,

 drugs, detergents and explosives.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Blue or roman vitriol is cupric sulfate (CuSO4).
 
• **Green vitriol is also called copperas**, a name formerly applied to all the vitriols is ferrous sulfate
 
• **White vitriol is zinc sulfate **(ZnSO4)**.**
 
• **Red, or rose, vitriol** is **cobalt sulfate **(CoSO4).
 
• **Uran vitriol** is a native **uranium sulfate **[U(SO4)2]**. **

questions.question: Which instrument records the waves reaching the surface during an earthquake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seismograph**__.

__
 
• Seismograph records the waves reaching the surface during an earthquake.

__
 
• **Earthquakes:**

 
 
• The sudden tremors or shaking of the earth's crust is called an **earthquake.**
 
• The earth’s crust is made up of different parts of various sizes. They are called plates.
 
• Most of the earthquakes in the world are caused by the movements of the plates.
 
• ‘**Seismology**’ deals with the study of the earthquake.
 
• ‘**Richter scale**’ and ‘**Mercalli scale**’ are the instruments to measure and record the magnitude and the intensity of an earthquake respectively.
 
 
 
• The place where the seismic waves originate** beneath the earth’s surface **is called the **focus of the earthquake**.
 
• The **epicenter **is that **point on the** **ground surface** that is closest to the focus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Earthquake Science Data Centre** is located in New Delhi.
 
• A **chronometer** is a portable** timekeeping device **of great accuracy.
 
• A **barograph **is a recording aneroid barometer where the **changes in atmospheric pressure** are recorded.
 
• A **Manometer **is a device to measure **pressures**.

questions.question: In which year did Motilal Nehru (Chairman) and eight other Congress leaders draft a constitution for India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

__
 
• In 1928 Motilal Nehru (Chairman) and eight other Congress leaders draft a constitution for India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nehru Report (1928 AD):**

 
 
• Nehru report was tabled in 1928 AD by **Motilal Nehru**.
 
• It remains memorable as the** first major Indian effort to draft a constitutional framework for India.**
 
• The recommendations evoked a debate concerning the goal of **India-Dominion status of complete independence.**
 
• Other members of the committee were Tej Bahadur Sapru, Ali Imam, M.S. Aney, Mangal Singh, Sohaib Qureshi, G.R. Pradhan and Subhash Chandra Bose.
 
 
 
• **Recommendations of the Nehru Report:**
 
 
• Dominion status
 
• Rejection of separate electorates.
 
• Linguistic provinces.
 
• Nineteen fundamental rights including equal rights fr women.
 
• Full protection to cultural and religious interests of Muslims.
 
• Complete dissociation of religion from the state. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jinnah’s 14 points (9th March 1929 AD):
 
 
• Jinnah, the leader of the Muslim League did not accept the Nehru Report and drew up a list of fourteen demands, which became famous as 14 points of Jinnah.

Prohibition of employment of children (Under the age of 14) in factories and mines
Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance.

__
 
• The provision of Article 49 of the Constitution of India Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy:
 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution from **Articles 36 to 51.**
 
• They embody the** concept of a welfare state.**
 
• These are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• They are** non-justifiable**.
 
• They apply to both **Union and State Governments** and all other authorities coming under the definition of ‘State’.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51**: To promote international peace and security and to maintain just and honourable relations between nations; to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and to encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
 
• **Article 45**: To provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
